name: Walter Jennings, Diabetic Foot Infection HD 3

caseMeta.title: Diabetic Foot Infection / Osteomyelitis - Hospital Day 3
learningObjectives: Perform and document a diabetic foot assessment (monofilament, pulses, ulcer size, probe-to-bone, erythema borders) and recognize signs of limb-threatening infection.
Safely administer vancomycin with piperacillin-tazobactam (infusion times, level timing, creatinine and allergy swaps) and obtain cultures before antibiotics.
Manage glucose in an infected, NPO and post-operative patient with basal-bolus insulin and a hypoglycemia protocol.
Provide offloading, open-wound and PICC care and teach foot protection, insulin and antibiotic adherence before discharge.
Connect assessment findings, labs and orders to prioritize nursing care.
Safely administer medications using the MAR and linked monitoring data.

orders.name: Renal, consistent carbohydrate diet
orders.instructions: Carbohydrate 60 g per meal; protein at every meal and a protein supplement twice daily for wound healing. Glucose check before every meal; mealtime insulin only when eating.

orders.name: NPO
orders.instructions: NPO after midnight for surgery; sips of water with essential medications allowed until 2 hours before. Glucose every 6 hours; basal insulin reduced 20%; mealtime insulin held.

orders.name: Renal, consistent carbohydrate diet
orders.instructions: Advance as tolerated once awake and not nauseated. Carbohydrate 60 g per meal; protein supplement twice daily.

orders.name: Bed rest, non-weight bearing right foot, right leg elevated
orders.instructions: No weight on the right foot at all (offloading): bedside commode with assistance, wheelchair for transport. Elevate on pillows with the heel floated; do not place pillows under the knee.

orders.name: Bed rest until nerve block wears off, then up with assistance
orders.instructions: Keep the foot elevated; check sensation, movement and toe color every hour until the block resolves.

orders.name: Heel weight bearing only right foot in post-operative shoe, walker, up with assistance
orders.instructions: No weight on the forefoot; use the offloading shoe for every transfer and every step. Gait belt, walker, call light in reach. Elevate the foot when seated or in bed.

orders.name: Right foot ulcer care: cleanse, moist dressing, offload
orders.instructions: Remove the old dressing; cleanse with normal saline (no povidone, peroxide or soaks); measure length x width x depth and probe for bone; document drainage color, amount, odor and surrounding erythema. Pack lightly with saline-moistened gauze, cover with dry gauze and a loose wrap. Keep both feet dry between the toes.
nursingConsiderations: Never soak diabetic feet; check water temperature because neuropathy hides burns.
Report foul odor, new black tissue, spreading redness, blisters, crepitus or a bright red or dusky toe.

orders.name: Mark erythema borders; measure; reassess every shift
orders.instructions: Outline the redness with a skin marker; record date, time, initials and size. Compare each shift. Notify provider if redness spreads past the line, or for new blisters, dusky skin, crepitus, fever or hypotension (necrotizing infection).

orders.name: Neurovascular checks right foot
orders.frequency: Every shift (every 4 hours for 24 hours after surgery)
orders.instructions: Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses (Doppler if not palpable), capillary refill, color, warmth, sensation and toe movement, compared with the other foot.
nursingConsiderations: Cool, pale or dusky toes or loss of Doppler signal: call the surgeon at once.

orders.name: Diabetic foot check and protection, both feet
orders.instructions: Inspect the opposite foot and heels including between the toes every shift; keep heels floated; no barefoot walking; padded footwear; monofilament and vibration findings documented. Loss of protective sensation: the patient cannot feel injury.

orders.name: Point-of-care blood glucose
orders.instructions: Check before meals and at bedtime; every 6 hours while NPO and with any symptoms. Goal 140-180 mg/dL. Notify the provider for glucose below 70 or above 300.

orders.name: Hypoglycemia protocol
orders.instructions: Awake and able to swallow: 15 g fast carbohydrate, recheck in 15 minutes, repeat until above 70, then a snack. NPO or unable to swallow: dextrose 50% IV (glucagon IM if no IV). Notify the provider.

orders.name: Blood cultures x2
orders.frequency: Once, before the first antibiotic dose
orders.instructions: Two sets from separate sites.

orders.name: Wound culture: deep tissue at debridement
orders.instructions: Send deep tissue (not a surface swab) for aerobic and anaerobic culture in a sterile container. Bone margin culture and pathology are sent from the OR.

orders.name: MRSA contact precautions
orders.instructions: MRSA-positive nares and wound: gown and gloves for contact with the patient and wound; dedicated equipment; hand hygiene with soap and water or alcohol rub; sign on the door.

orders.name: Verify tetanus immunization
orders.instructions: Give Tdap if the last booster was more than 5 years ago or unknown (open wound).

orders.name: Fall precautions (neuropathy, non-weight bearing, opioid)
orders.instructions: Bed alarm, assist x1-2 for every transfer, offloading shoe on for every step, gait belt, call light in reach.

orders.name: Nutrition consult: protein and calorie needs for wound healing
orders.instructions: Dietitian to assess; albumin and prealbumin ordered; protein target about 1.2-1.5 g/kg unless kidney disease.

orders.name: Diabetes education
orders.instructions: Insulin teaching (basal-bolus), glucometer, hypoglycemia treatment, daily foot checks, proper footwear. Teach-back.

orders.name: Pre-operative checklist, consent and site verification
orders.instructions: Verify consent, ID and allergy bands, right foot marked, NPO status, glucose within range (goal below 180), last antibiotic dose, last dose of insulin, and that blood thinners have been held per surgeon.

orders.name: Surgical dressing and open-wound care, first ray amputation site
orders.frequency: Every shift check; dressing change daily by surgeon/RN
orders.instructions: First dressing change by the surgeon on post-operative day 1. Then: remove packing, irrigate with normal saline, pack loosely with moist saline gauze, cover with ABD and loose wrap. Measure and document wound size, color of tissue, drainage and odor. Premedicate for pain 30-60 minutes before.
nursingConsiderations: Strikethrough drainage: mark and time the drainage and tell the surgeon; report a dusky flap or foul odor.

orders.name: Physical therapy evaluation and treatment
orders.instructions: Transfers and walker gait with heel weight bearing right foot in the offloading shoe; stairs if needed at home.

orders.name: Renal dosing review / avoid nephrotoxins
orders.instructions: Pharmacy to renally dose medications. Avoid NSAIDs, IV contrast when possible, and other nephrotoxic agents.
nursingConsiderations: Question any NSAID or contrast order and notify the provider.

orders.name: Skin assessment with attention to skin folds
orders.instructions: Inspect skin folds, sacrum, and heels for moisture and pressure injury.

orders.name: Bariatric / appropriate-size equipment and lift assist
orders.instructions: Use appropriately rated bed, chair and lift equipment; at least 2 staff for mobilization.

orders.name: Lower extremity circulation checks (pulses, color, temperature, capillary refill)
orders.instructions: Compare both legs: dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses (Doppler if not palpable), color, temperature, cap refill, sensation. Report a new cool, pale or painful limb immediately (acute limb ischemia).

orders.name: Foot and heel protection
orders.instructions: Inspect feet and heels for wounds or color change; float heels, loose heel-offloading boots; no heating pads or tight stockings.

orders.name: Avoid sequential compression devices and compression stockings (ABI 0.45)
orders.instructions: Moderate-severe PAD: compression can cause limb ischemia. Use pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis; SCDs only if vascular surgery clears them.

orders.name: Tobacco cessation counseling
orders.instructions: Offer cessation counseling and quitline information before discharge.

orders.name: Vital signs
orders.instructions: Notify provider for SBP below 90 or above 180, HR above 120 or below 50, RR above 28, SpO2 below 90%, or temperature above 101.5 F.

orders.name: Strict intake and output
orders.instructions: Record all oral and IV intake and all output (urine, drains, emesis).

orders.name: Continuous pulse oximetry while on opioids
orders.instructions: Notify provider for SpO2 below 90% or RR below 10.

orders.name: X-ray right foot, 3 views
orders.instructions: Perform X-ray right foot, 3 views.
orders.rationale: Diabetic plantar ulcer with swelling and drainage: exclude osteomyelitis, gas or foreign body

orders.name: Arterial studies right leg: ankle-brachial index, toe pressures and waveforms
orders.instructions: Perform Arterial studies right leg: ankle-brachial index, toe pressures and waveforms.
orders.rationale: Diabetic foot ulcer: assess perfusion for healing and level of amputation

orders.name: Consult: Podiatry / Foot and Ankle Surgery
orders.instructions: Diabetic foot infection with probable osteomyelitis

orders.name: Consult: Infectious Diseases
orders.instructions: Diabetic foot osteomyelitis: antibiotic selection and duration

orders.name: MRI right foot without and with contrast
orders.instructions: Perform MRI right foot without and with contrast.
orders.rationale: Probe-to-bone positive ulcer: confirm and map osteomyelitis for surgical planning

orders.name: Consult: Vascular Surgery
orders.instructions: Peripheral arterial disease in a diabetic with a foot wound

orders.name: Right first ray amputation (great toe and first metatarsal head), open
orders.instructions: Right first ray amputation (great toe and first metatarsal head), open. Consent, NPO status and pre-op checklist before transport.
orders.rationale: Osteomyelitis of the first metatarsal head and great toe with plantar abscess
nursingConsiderations: Confirm consent is signed and in chart.
Confirm NPO status and last intake time.
Complete pre-op checklist; verify allergy band and site marking.

orders.name: 12-lead ECG
orders.instructions: Perform 12-lead ECG.

orders.name: CBC and comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP)
orders.instructions: Draw at 0500 daily. CBC plus CMP (sodium, potassium, chloride, CO2, BUN, creatinine, glucose, calcium, AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, albumin, total protein). Admission labs were drawn in the ED; the first routine AM draw is 2026-10-20 at 0500.

orders.name: Magnesium and phosphorus
orders.instructions: Draw with the 0500 labs. Replace per protocol (magnesium goal 2.0 or higher with arrhythmia risk).

orders.name: Platelet and kidney monitoring for heparin / low-molecular-weight heparin
orders.instructions: Platelets are checked every 2-3 days for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (a fall of 50% or to below 100); creatinine is checked because enoxaparin is cleared by the kidneys. Hold and call for active bleeding or platelets below 50.

orders.name: Potassium and creatinine monitoring for diuretic / ACE inhibitor / ARB
orders.instructions: Report potassium below 3.5 or above 5.0, or a creatinine rise of 0.3 or more. Hold ACE inhibitor/ARB and call for SBP below 100 or rising creatinine/potassium.

orders.name: Vancomycin trough or AUC
orders.frequency: Before the 4th dose, then per pharmacy
orders.instructions: Draw 30 minutes before the dose. Pharmacy adjusts the dose; monitor creatinine daily.

orders.name: vancomycin IVPB
orders.instructions: Administer 1,000 mg IV Every 24 hours. Hold and call pharmacy/provider for creatinine rise of 0.3 mg/dL or more, urine output drop, or vancomycin level above 20 mcg/mL.
orders.rationale: MRSA diabetic foot osteomyelitis (IV through 6 weeks if bone margin positive)
nursingConsiderations: Interval extended for reduced GFR; pharmacy doses by level/AUC.
Hold and call pharmacy/provider for creatinine rise of 0.3 mg/dL or more, urine output drop, or vancomycin level above 20 mcg/mL.

medication.importantInfo: Infuse over at least 90-120 minutes (no faster than 1 g/hr) to avoid vancomycin infusion reaction (flushing, itching, hypotension). Dosed by AUC (goal 400-600) or trough. Nephrotoxic and ototoxic, and kidney injury risk rises when given with piperacillin-tazobactam: monitor creatinine and urine output daily; report ringing in the ears.
medication.hold: Hold and call pharmacy/provider for creatinine rise of 0.3 mg/dL or more, urine output drop, or vancomycin level above 20 mcg/mL.

orders.name: meropenem IVPB
orders.instructions: Administer 1 g IV Every 12 hours.
nursingConsiderations: Dose adjusted for reduced GFR.

medication.importantInfo: Used because of penicillin allergy (low cross-reactivity). Infuse over 30 minutes; may lower seizure threshold in renal impairment. Does not cover MRSA: vancomycin continues.

orders.name: multivitamin with minerals tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1 tablet Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Supports wound healing. High-protein oral supplement ordered by the dietitian.

orders.name: aspirin chewable tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 81 mg Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Monitor for bleeding. Continue through surgery unless surgeon directs otherwise.

orders.name: nicotine (NICODERM CQ) 24 hour patch
orders.instructions: Administer 14 mg Transdermal Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Rotate sites; remove old patch. Do not smoke while wearing patch.

orders.name: insulin lispro (HUMALOG) injection
orders.instructions: Administer Correction scale only (moderate-dose) Subcutaneous Every 6 hours. Hold mealtime dose if not eating or glucose below 70 mg/dL; call provider.
orders.rationale: Type 2 diabetes: mealtime and correction insulin
nursingConsiderations: Dose reduced about 25% for reduced kidney function.
Hold mealtime dose if not eating or glucose below 70 mg/dL; call provider.

medication.importantInfo: Mealtime dose given 0-15 minutes BEFORE eating plus correction by scale. Check glucose first and document it. Hold the mealtime dose if the patient eats less than half the meal (correction only).
medication.hold: Hold mealtime dose if not eating or glucose below 70 mg/dL; call provider.

orders.name: acetaminophen (TYLENOL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 650 mg Oral Every 6 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Scheduled base of pain control; maximum 3 g per 24 hours from all sources. Record the temperature before giving so it does not mask a fever trend. Avoid NSAIDs (kidney injury with vancomycin).

orders.name: ertapenem (INVANZ) IVPB
orders.instructions: Administer 500 mg IV Every 24 hours.
nursingConsiderations: Dose halved for CrCl 30 or below.

medication.importantInfo: Used because of penicillin/cephalosporin allergy; once daily dosing suits home infusion. Infuse over 30 minutes. Seizure risk in renal impairment.

orders.name: insulin glargine (LANTUS) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 22 units Subcutaneous Nightly at bedtime. Notify provider before giving if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.
orders.rationale: Type 2 diabetes: basal insulin, glucose goal 140-180 mg/dL
nursingConsiderations: Dose reduced about 25% for reduced kidney function.
Notify provider before giving if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.

medication.importantInfo: Basal insulin (about 0.25 units/kg). Give even when NPO, at 80% of the dose. Check glucose first; call the provider before giving if glucose is below 100 mg/dL. Infection and stress raise needs now; doses fall as the infection is controlled.
medication.hold: Notify provider before giving if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.

orders.name: lisinopril (PRINIVIL,ZESTRIL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 20 mg Oral Daily. Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.

medication.importantInfo: Check BP before giving. Monitor potassium and creatinine. Watch for cough and angioedema.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.

orders.name: atorvastatin (LIPITOR) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg Oral Nightly at bedtime.

medication.importantInfo: Report unexplained muscle pain or weakness.

orders.name: cilostazol (PLETAL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 100 mg Oral BID. Hold and notify provider for HR above 110, palpitations or new dyspnea/edema.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider for HR above 110, palpitations or new dyspnea/edema.

medication.importantInfo: Give 30 minutes before or 2 hours after meals. For claudication. CONTRAINDICATED in heart failure; may cause headache, diarrhea and palpitations.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider for HR above 110, palpitations or new dyspnea/edema.

orders.name: enoxaparin (LOVENOX) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg Subcutaneous Daily. Hold and notify provider for active bleeding or platelets below 50.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider for active bleeding or platelets below 50.

medication.importantInfo: Monitor for bleeding, bruising, platelets and renal function. Never give if platelets below 50 or active bleeding.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider for active bleeding or platelets below 50.

orders.name: senna-docusate (SENOKOT-S) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 2 tablets Oral BID.

medication.importantInfo: Hold for loose stools. Goal: a bowel movement at least every other day.

orders.name: lactated Ringer's infusion
orders.instructions: Administer 75 mL/hr IV Continuous at 75 mL/hr.

medication.importantInfo: Assess lungs, edema, I&O and daily weight. Check IV site each shift.

orders.name: dextrose 50% injection
orders.frequency: Every 15 minutes PRN glucose below 70 mg/dL when NPO or unable to swallow
orders.instructions: Administer 25 mL (12.5 g) IV Every 15 minutes PRN glucose below 70 mg/dL when NPO or unable to swallow.

medication.importantInfo: Per hypoglycemia protocol; recheck glucose in 15 minutes and repeat if below 70. Notify the provider of any glucose below 70.

orders.name: glucagon injection
orders.frequency: Every 15 minutes PRN glucose below 70 mg/dL with no IV access and unable to swallow
orders.instructions: Administer 1 mg IM Every 15 minutes PRN glucose below 70 mg/dL with no IV access and unable to swallow.

medication.importantInfo: Per hypoglycemia protocol. Turn the patient on the side; vomiting can follow.

orders.name: oxycodone (ROXICODONE) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 5 mg Oral Every 4 hours PRN moderate pain (4-6). Hold for RR below 10 or sedation.
nursingConsiderations: Hold for RR below 10 or sedation.

medication.importantInfo: HIGH-ALERT. Neuropathy dulls pain, but surgical wounds still hurt. Assess pain and sedation before and 30-60 minutes after. Premedicate 30-60 minutes before dressing changes. Hold for RR below 10 or oversedation.
medication.hold: Hold for RR below 10 or sedation.

orders.name: hydromorphone (DILAUDID) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 0.25 mg IV Every 3 hours PRN severe pain (7-10). Hold for RR below 10, SpO2 below 90%, or sedation.
nursingConsiderations: Hold for RR below 10, SpO2 below 90%, or sedation.

medication.importantInfo: HIGH-ALERT. Assess pain, sedation (RASS), RR and SpO2 before and 15-30 minutes after. Hold for RR below 10 or oversedation.
medication.hold: Hold for RR below 10, SpO2 below 90%, or sedation.

orders.name: ondansetron (ZOFRAN) injection
orders.frequency: Every 8 hours PRN nausea or vomiting
orders.instructions: Administer 4 mg IV Every 8 hours PRN nausea or vomiting.

medication.importantInfo: May prolong QT; check ECG/electrolytes if other QT-prolonging drugs. Reassess nausea in 30 minutes.

orders.name: vancomycin IVPB
orders.instructions: Administer 2,750 mg IV Once.

medication.importantInfo: Weight-based loading dose (25 mg/kg), given after blood cultures. Infuse over at least 90-120 minutes (no faster than 1 g/hr) to avoid vancomycin infusion reaction (flushing, itching, hypotension). Dosed by AUC (goal 400-600) or trough. Nephrotoxic and ototoxic, and kidney injury risk rises when given with piperacillin-tazobactam: monitor creatinine and urine output daily; report ringing in the ears.

orders.name: lactated Ringer's bolus
orders.instructions: Administer 1,000 mL IV Once.
orders.rationale: Dehydration from hyperglycemia and sepsis physiology (lactate 2.1)
nursingConsiderations: Stop the bolus and notify provider for new crackles, dyspnea or SpO2 drop.

medication.importantInfo: Reassess vital signs, lung sounds and urine output after the bolus.

orders.name: insulin lispro (HUMALOG) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 8 units Subcutaneous Once.

medication.importantInfo: One-time correction for glucose 342 in the ED. Recheck glucose in 2 hours.

orders.name: lisinopril (PRINIVIL,ZESTRIL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 20 mg Oral Daily. Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.

medication.importantInfo: Check BP before giving. Monitor potassium and creatinine. Watch for cough and angioedema.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.

orders.name: atorvastatin (LIPITOR) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg Oral Nightly at bedtime.

medication.importantInfo: Report unexplained muscle pain or weakness.

orders.name: heparin injection
orders.instructions: Administer 5,000 units Subcutaneous Every 8 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Monitor for bleeding, bruising, platelets and renal function. Never give if platelets below 50 or active bleeding.

orders.name: senna-docusate (SENOKOT-S) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 2 tablets Oral BID.

medication.importantInfo: Hold for loose stools. Goal: a bowel movement at least every other day.

stickyNotes.title: To OR
stickyNotes.body: OR about 0800: NPO, glucose below 180, basal insulin at 80%, consent, right foot marked, antibiotics on schedule.

stickyNotes.title: Diabetic foot: offloading
stickyNotes.body: Non-weight bearing right foot until surgery, then heel weight bearing only in the offloading shoe. Check BOTH feet every shift; neuropathy hides injury.

stickyNotes.title: MRSA contact precautions
stickyNotes.body: MRSA in the nares and wound: gown and gloves for wound care and room entry.

stickyNotes.title: Insulin safety
stickyNotes.body: Basal insulin is NOT skipped when NPO (give 80% of the dose). Mealtime insulin only when eating; correction scale every 6 hours while NPO. Treat glucose below 70 per protocol.

stickyNotes.title: Vancomycin monitoring
stickyNotes.body: Infuse over at least 90 minutes; level before the 4th dose and weekly; creatinine and urine output daily (kidney injury risk rises with piperacillin-tazobactam). Report ringing in the ears.

stickyNotes.title: Coming up this shift
stickyNotes.body: 0800 Right first ray amputation (great toe and first metatarsal head), open.

notes.title: Brief Operative Note
notes.author: R. Alvarez, MD
notes.summary: Right first ray amputation (great toe and first metatarsal head), open: no complications; to PACU, then medical unit.
notes.body:
**Pre-operative diagnosis**
- Osteomyelitis of the first metatarsal head and great toe with plantar abscess

**Post-operative diagnosis**
- Osteomyelitis of the first metatarsal head and great toe with plantar abscess

**Procedure**
- Right first ray amputation (great toe and first metatarsal head), open

**Surgeon / anesthesia**
- R. Alvarez, MD; Popliteal and saphenous nerve block with monitored anesthesia care

**Findings**
- Purulent plantar abscess tracking along the first metatarsal head; infected, soft, discolored bone. Metatarsal cut back to firm bleeding bone; wound left open for infection control.

**Description**
Block placed and sedation given. Wound irrigated and the abscess debrided. Great toe disarticulated and the first metatarsal head and distal shaft resected with a saw. Proximal metatarsal margin sent separately for culture and pathology. Pulsed irrigation with 3 L saline. Wound packed with moist gauze and loosely dressed; plantar skin flap preserved for delayed closure.

**EBL / fluids**
- EBL 30 mL; IV fluids 500 mL lactated Ringer's

**Specimens**
- First ray to pathology; proximal bone margin to pathology and culture

**Complications**
- None

**Disposition**
- PACU, then medical unit; stable.

notes.title: Bedside sharp debridement of right plantar foot ulcer with deep tissue culture
notes.author: R. Alvarez, MD
notes.summary: Bedside debridement right foot ulcer
notes.body:
**Procedure**
- Bedside sharp debridement of right plantar foot ulcer with deep tissue culture

**Indication**
- Purulent diabetic foot ulcer with probable osteomyelitis

**Findings / technique**
Time-out done. Neuropathic foot: no local anesthetic needed beyond topical. Ulcer 3.0 x 2.4 cm and 0.8 cm deep under the first metatarsal head. Callus and necrotic slough excised to bleeding tissue; pocket of thick yellow pus drained and the probe reaches rough bone. Deep tissue sent for aerobic and anaerobic culture. Irrigated with 1 L normal saline. Packed with moist saline gauze and dressed; foot elevated.

**Complications**
- None apparent. Patient tolerated the procedure; post-procedure vitals stable.

notes.title: Infectious Diseases Consult
notes.author: A. Rahman, MD (Infectious Diseases)
notes.summary: Infectious Diseases consulted
notes.body:
**Reason for consult**
- Diabetic foot osteomyelitis: antibiotic selection and duration

**Recommendations**
- Moderate-severe diabetic foot infection with probable osteomyelitis (ESR 98, bone erosion on x-ray, probe-to-bone positive). Continue vancomycin (AUC-guided) plus piperacillin-tazobactam until deep cultures finalize, then narrow. Get deep tissue and proximal bone margin cultures. If the proximal bone margin is clean: 2-5 more days after amputation. If the margin is positive for osteomyelitis: 6 weeks of IV antibiotics through a PICC with weekly CBC, BMP, ESR/CRP and vancomycin level, and ID clinic follow-up.

notes.title: Hospitalist History and Physical
notes.author: S. Patel, MD
notes.summary: Admission H&P for diabetic foot infection with osteomyelitis.
notes.body:
**Chief complaint**
- Right foot ulcer with redness, swelling, drainage and fever

**History of present illness**
61-year-old male with long-standing type 2 diabetes (home glucose in the 300s for a week) and peripheral neuropathy, sent to the ED with a 3-week-old ulcer under the ball of the right foot that now has foul-smelling drainage, redness spreading over the forefoot, swelling of the great toe, chills and a temperature of 101.4 F. The ulcer began after new shoes; the patient felt no pain from it and kept walking on it. No chest pain, dyspnea, vomiting, abdominal pain or confusion. No antibiotics before arrival. Last foot exam by a clinician more than a year ago.

**Past medical history**
- Chronic kidney disease stage 3; Obesity (BMI 34.1); Type 2 diabetes mellitus (A1c 8.0%); Hypertension; Hyperlipidemia; Peripheral arterial disease (claudication, ABI 0.45)

**Past surgical history**
- No prior surgeries.

**Home medications**
- insulin glargine (LANTUS) 20 units Subcutaneous Nightly at bedtime
- insulin lispro (HUMALOG) correction scale Low-dose correction scale Subcutaneous ACHS (before meals and at bedtime)
- lisinopril (PRINIVIL,ZESTRIL) 20 mg Oral Daily
- atorvastatin (LIPITOR) 40 mg Oral Nightly at bedtime
- aspirin chewable 81 mg Oral Daily
- cilostazol (PLETAL) 100 mg Oral BID
- (Metformin held while hospitalized (contrast, acute illness, renal risk).)

**Allergies**
- Penicillin (Hives)

**Family history**
- Mother with hypertension and type 2 diabetes; father with coronary artery disease. Mother and a brother with type 2 diabetes; brother had a toe amputation.

**Social history**

61-year-old male with a history of chronic kidney disease stage 3, obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, peripheral arterial disease admitted with diabetic foot infection with osteomyelitis.

**Peripheral arterial disease**
- Continue antiplatelet and statin; limb checks every shift.
- No SCDs or compression stockings; pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis; protect heels.

notes.title: X-ray right foot, 3 views
notes.author: W. Chen, MD (Radiology)
notes.summary: Findings concerning for osteomyelitis of the first metatarsal head and great toe proximal phalanx. No soft tissue gas.
notes.body:
**Indication**
- Diabetic plantar ulcer with swelling and drainage: exclude osteomyelitis, gas or foreign body

**Technique**
- X-ray right foot, 3 views.

**Findings**
Plantar soft tissue defect beneath the first metatarsal head with surrounding soft tissue swelling. Cortical erosion and periosteal reaction of the right first metatarsal head and proximal phalanx base of the great toe. No subcutaneous gas or radiopaque foreign body. Dense vascular calcification of the dorsalis pedis and plantar arteries. No Charcot deformity.

**Impression**
- Findings concerning for osteomyelitis of the first metatarsal head and great toe proximal phalanx. No soft tissue gas.
